games.reasoning: No read: the line is unchanged from the open, and every finding (Houston 4-0, Milwaukee's rebuild, Houston's weak bench) was public when the number was set. [angle] Covers preview (Oct 28): without Edwards last season Minnesota went 12-9 SU and 13-8 ATS. Its defensive rating improved from 115 to 109.5 while its offensive rating fell from 117.6 to 115. Helps Wolves.
Covers preview (Oct 28): the Wolves have covered all four games to open this season. Helps Wolves; ATS record, tiebreaker only.
Covers preview (Oct 28): Golden State ranks 28th in defensive rating, and its frontcourt lacks size and depth. Helps Wolves.

Covers preview (Oct 28): Rudy Gobert has 12+ rebounds in three of four games (14.3 avg). The writer's top pick is Wolves -3.5 (good up to -4.5) on frontcourt length (Kuminga, McDaniels, Gobert). Helps Wolves.

Covers ATS and moneyline columns (Oct 28): Golden State creates more wide-open threes and allows fewer. Minnesota ranks 25th in assist rate and is easier to defend in isolation without Edwards. Helps Warriors.
Covers (Oct 28): Curry has 25+ points in five straight games and averages 26 against Minnesota in his career. Helps Warriors.

[angle] Covers (Oct 28): Ayo Dosunmu is expected to start and averaged 29.4 PRA in seven games without Edwards last season; Kuminga has started four straight. The Wolves' replacement pieces are known.
Dimers model (Oct 28): Wolves 116-111, with Wolves -3.5 covering 50.5% of the time. That puts the line on the number.
Total stayed at 227.5 from open to close (slate file). Neutral.
games.reasoning: After a 3-point injury move the lessons say to treat the new number as fair, and the two Covers writers split on the side. My projection of Wolves by 3.5 sits on the line, so it's a pass. Forced side Minnesota: its defense was better without Edwards last season (109.5), and Golden State's defense ranks 28th this season. Confirmation that Minnesota's interior was healthy would have made it a lean.

Covers preview (Oct 28): Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic are out, and Markkanen (wrist) is expected to miss. Helps Spurs.

[angle] Covers (Oct 28): San Antonio is on the second night of a back-to-back after blowing out Sacramento on Tuesday. Last season the Spurs went 11-4 ATS on no rest (+6.2). The back-to-back helps the Jazz, though that ATS record leans Spurs.
Covers ATS column (Oct 28): Utah is 0-4 ATS this season and has faced only one projected winning team. Helps Spurs; ATS record, tiebreaker only.
Covers preview (Oct 28): the Spurs' two wins came by 16 and 27, they lead the league in scoring margin (+15.1), and they allow 109.8 a game. Helps Spurs.

Covers preview (Oct 28): the Spurs are 4-0 ATS in their last four games at Utah. Venue history, already priced.
Both Covers writers took the Spurs (-12.5 and -13.5). Preview picks aren't an edge.
games.reasoning: Projecting the close (Spurs by 13.5) gives a 2-point gap to the slate's 11.5. Shaded halfway to the line it's 1 point, under the bar, and the lessons call a slate line better than the close information, not an edge (4-3). The Spurs' back-to-back against a depleted frontcourt makes it a pass. Forced side Spurs: Utah's frontcourt is thin against Wembanyama, the market moved that way, and the slate number is 2 points better.

[angle] WagerTalk (Oct 28): public spread money is on Dallas, while the line still moved toward Dallas. Helps Mavs slightly.

A confirmed Kyrie return would have pushed it toward a lean.
